title: cosyte drift manifest
description: The shape of drift-manifest.json, which IS the cosyte engineering baseline. Validated by scripts/validate-drift-manifest.mjs, which implements the subset of JSON Schema used here and nothing more: a manifest that needs a keyword the validator does not know is a change to BOTH files. The subset is type, required, properties, additionalProperties, patternProperties, propertyNames, items, minItems, minProperties, minLength, minimum, uniqueItems, enum, const, pattern and local $ref into $defs. No remote references: this file must validate with no network and no node_modules.

$schema.description: The schema this manifest is validated against, resolved relative to the manifest.

manifestVersion.description: 2 is the re-derived, two-baseline shape. 1 was the flat, single-target shape whose authority was a prose document that no longer exists.

standing.description: What this file's authority IS. It may not defer to a prose document, because the last one it deferred to was deleted and took the provenance of every requirement with it.

baselines.description: Exactly two, and together they cover the whole estate. The operator refused both `one baseline for all 24 repos` and `only the 13 with the rest excluded`.

phiScanProbeComment.description: Why the phi-scan check is a capability probe and not a matcher. Carried unchanged from manifest version 1.

installHardeningProbeComment.description: Why scripts/install-hardening.mjs exists as a separate gate, and what was MEASURED rather than assumed about the pinned pnpm.

repoName.description: A submodule PATH from the umbrella's .gitmodules, never a submodule NAME. The pattern is load-bearing: the org profile repo is NAMED `.github` and PATHED `github-profile`, the checker resolves a repo by joining the umbrella root with the name it is given, and the umbrella root has its own `.github/` directory. A leading dot cannot be written here, so that repo cannot be addressed by name even by accident.

provenance.description: Where this group's requirements were DERIVED from. Not a description of what they are: a claim about their source, so a later reader can argue with it. The floor is long enough that a placeholder cannot satisfy it.

addressedBy.description: Repos are addressed by PATH. The enum has one member so that widening it is a deliberate edit here.

submodulePaths.description: Every submodule path in the umbrella. Each one must be claimed by exactly one baseline; the validator enforces that, and it is how `every repo owes something` stops being a claim.

ceiling.description: What this baseline may NOT grow to cover, where an operator decision set one.

missingPackageJson.description: What the checker does with a repo that is present but carries no package.json. `skip` is the version-1 greenfield behaviour and is right for a baseline made of npm packages; `evaluate` is required for a baseline whose repos mostly have no package.json at all, where skipping would silently clear nearly every one of them.

groups.description: Requirement groups. Every one carries its own provenance, so a requirement can never again be inherited from a document nobody can read.

requirements.description: One or more requirement kinds. The kind names are a CLOSED set, shared with the evaluator table in scripts/drift-check.js: a kind the checker cannot evaluate must not be expressible here, or the manifest would declare a requirement nothing grades.

devDepVersions.description: Wanted version prefixes, matched part by part. An empty string means presence only.

caretAllowed.description: Dependency names exempt from the exact-pin rule.

caretAllowedScopes.description: Name prefixes exempt from the exact-pin rule. A parameter of `caretAllowed`, which is the requirement that reads it; declared here because it was hardcoded in the checker before.

packageJsonEquals.description: Dotted paths into package.json that must hold the given value.

agentDoc.description: SHAPE ONLY. Presence of the file, presence of the declared headings, and a line ceiling. Nothing here may describe CONTENT: the operator overturned decision 15 for shape alone, and the checker is written so that no line other than a heading is read, reported or asserted.

files.description: Accepted agent-context filenames, canonical first. The first one present is the one graded; when none is present the canonical name is what the drift line reports.

requiredHeadings.description: A heading matches when the file carries a heading line that STARTS WITH this text, so a repo may qualify its own headings.

phiScanCapabilityProbe.description: Run the repo's own scanner against a synthetic corpus. Parameters live in the top-level phiScanProbe key.

pnpmInstallHardening.description: The two pnpm resolution controls that defend a repo's INSTALL rather than its build: a publication cooldown and a no-downgrade trust policy, both read out of the repo's pnpm settings file. Both ship switched OFF at pnpm 10, so a repo that does not declare them does not have them.

settingsFile.description: The repo-relative file pnpm reads these settings from. pnpm's documented examples put them in pnpm-workspace.yaml, and .npmrc is not among the routes pnpm names for configuring them explicitly.

minimumReleaseAgeMinutes.description: The floor in minutes. A repo declaring MORE than this satisfies the requirement; a repo declaring less does not.

trustPolicy.description: The exact value required. `off` is pnpm's default and is not a policy.

optionalWorkflows.description: The workflows the estate CARRIES that no baseline REQUIRES. Declared rather than left to silence: the checker only asks whether a required workflow is present, so an undeclared extra is tolerated without anything saying it was considered. A workflow named here is not drift when a repo carries it and not a missing requirement when a repo does not, and scripts/drift-check.js prints the set in every report. The validator refuses a workflow that appears both here and in some baseline's requiredWorkflows, so `optional` and `required` cannot be claimed of the same file.

workflow.description: The workflow FILENAME, in the same vocabulary requiredWorkflows uses, so that `optional here` and `required there` are comparable strings rather than two spellings of one idea.

carriedBy.description: The repos measured as carrying it. Each must be a repo some baseline holds, which the validator enforces, so a carrier list cannot outlive the repo it names.

installHardeningProbe.description: Parameters for scripts/install-hardening.mjs, which grades THIS repository rather than a target. It sits here for the same reason phiScanProbe does: it is an argument to a check, not a requirement of a repo.

supportedFrom.description: The pnpm release each setting was added in. A pnpm older than this ignores the key entirely, which is a settings file that decorates rather than defends, and is one of the four states the gate refuses on.

phiScanProbe.description: Parameters for the one BEHAVIOURAL check. Carried unchanged from manifest version 1: changing what the probe asks is out of scope for a re-derivation, and loosening it turns a PHI-detection assertion into a vacuous pass across every PHI-bearing repo.

perRepo.description: Overrides for a repo whose scanner does not read the default fixture. The validator refuses an entry for a repo no baseline names, so an override cannot outlive its repo.

reDerivation.description: The record of what this file used to require and what became of it. Every key the previous manifest carried is accounted for here, so no requirement can vanish unmentioned.

preChangeKeys.description: Every top-level key the pre-change manifest carried. The validator requires each one to appear in exactly one of carriedUnchanged or droppedOrChanged.

carriedUnchanged.description: Keys whose requirement survived re-derivation with its value intact. The validator refuses one that is no longer present anywhere in this file, so this list cannot become a claim about a requirement that was quietly deleted.
